newsitem.title: ITALY: Trial sought for Italy's Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Trial sought for Italy's Prodi.

text.p: An Italian magistrate recommended on Monday that Prime Minister Romano Prodi should be tried for alleged abuse of office and conflict of interest during his chairmanship of giant state holding company IRI.
Prodi, who has led a centre-left government since May, reacted calmly to the news, telling journalists he had done no wrong and had full confidence in Italy's judicial system.

"The indictment request certainly does not put my personal honesty at stake," Prodi told a news conference in the northeast town of Udine, where he was on a visit. "It doesn't worry me and it doesn't put me in difficulty."
Prodi was later heckled by right-wing demonstrators in the town of Trieste who seized on the case to yell "thief" and "go to prison" at the 57-year-old former economist.

The requested indictment, lodged with court officials in Rome by deputy public prosecutor Giuseppa Geremia, relates to alleged irregularities in the sale by IRI in October 1993 of food company Cirio to a southern consortium, Fis.Vi.
Italian news agencies said Geremia's inquiry had concluded that Fis.Vi had gained an "unjust advantage" in the purchase as a result of favourable terms applied by IRI's board.

They said Geremia had asked for Prodi, five other members of the then board of IRI, including senior Treasury official Mario Draghi, and Fis.Vi director Carlo Saverio Lamiranda to be charged with complicity in abuse of office.

Prodi was also suspected of a conflict of interest by taking part in the decision on the sale despite a previous advisory role at the Anglo-Dutch group Unilever. The group had expressed an interest in Cirio and bought its edible oil business from Fis.Vi shortly after the IRI decision, the agency reports said.

Geremia's recommendation must be reviewed by an examining judge, Edoardo Landi, who will decide whether to indict the suspects and order a trial. The abuse of office offence carries a jail sentence of two to five years in the event of conviction.
Landi can also decide to drop the case or order further enquiries. The date of the hearing was not immediately known.
Government supporters, trade unions and the main opposition said the move would have no immediate effect on Prodi's tenure.
"I am sorry that a request has been made for prime minister Romano Prodi to stand trial," centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said in a statement.

Berlusconi, advised while he was prime minister in 1994 that he was suspected of bribery and now charged in two separate trials, said it was necessary "to await all future developments in the judicial case before expressing any judgment".
Prodi, who entered politics only in 1995, was chairman of IRI for most of the 1980s and again for a year from May 1993.

Geremia's investigation into the Cirio sale, part of a privatisation drive initiated by Prodi, began in February after a complaint from a small shareholder and questions in parliament from the opposition hard-right National Alliance party.
Fis.Vi bought 62 percent of Cirio from IRI for 310 billion lire ($206 million) but no longer owns the food company.
National Alliance leader Gianfranco Fini said the transaction had raised eyebrows in 1993 because Fis.Vi was not known to have significant financial resources.

"It is an affair that should not be minimised because I think that we have to understand out of a duty of elementary transparency whether IRI decided the sale to do someone a political favour," Fini told reporters.
